sentences.text: Miotadorna was an extinct genus of tadornine ducks that lived in New Zealand during the Miocene epoch.
This bird belongs to the family Anatidae and is classified within the subfamily Tadorninae.
The genus name Miotadorna indicates that the describers viewed the bird as a Miocene shelduck similar to modern Tadorna.
M. catrionae is the largest duck species discovered in the St Bathans fossil deposits.
This species is distinguished by its larger size and differing proportions compared to M. sanctibathansi.
The type species of the genus Miotadorna is Miotadorna sanctibathansi, which was described by Worthy et al. in 2007.

M. sanctibathansi was described from a fossilized right humerus found in the Saint Bathans Fauna within the lower Bannockburn Formation of the Manuherikia Group in the Central Otago region of New Zealand's South Island.
Miotadorna catrionae was synonymized with Miotadorna sanctibathansi by Tennyson et al. in 2022.
Miotadorna lived between 18.7 and 15.9 million years ago, spanning the Burdigalian to Langhian stages.

Researchers suggest the size difference between M. catrionae and M. sanctibathansi may represent sexual dimorphism, though this explanation is not fully supported by the morphological evidence. Worthy et al. (2022) considered M. catrionae a synonym of M. sanctibathansi, believing the larger specimen represented a larger sex rather than a distinct species.
